title: Temperature along a conducting copper rod
caption: In steady state the temperature falls linearly along the rod, 100 °C to 20 °C over 0.5 m: a gradient of 160 K m⁻¹. Heat flows down the gradient at P = κAΔT/L = 400 × 1 × 10⁻⁴ × 80/0.5 = 6.4 W. A straight line means the same heat flows through every cross-section.
alt: Graph of temperature against distance along the rod: a straight line from 100 °C at 0 m to 20 °C at 0.5 m, gradient −160 K per metre.
description: The horizontal axis is the distance along the rod in metres; the vertical axis is the temperature in °C.
The hot end is at 100 °C and the cold end at 20 °C, 0.5 m away.
The profile is a straight line of gradient −ΔT/L = −160 K m⁻¹, so P = κA × 160 = 400 × 1 × 10⁻⁴ × 160 = 6.4 W.
